-------------------------------------------------------------Project Summary------ -------------------------------------------------------
Epilepsy is a common neurological disorder that affects approximately 50 million people worldwide and a third of
these patients do not achieve adequate seizure control.

Only ~50% of epilepsies can be controlled with currently-

crippling epileptic seizures, resulting in profound loss of memory and cognitive function. The voltage-gated Na+
channel, NaV1.6 is encoded by the SCN8A gene, and is a particularly compelling therapeutic candidate for treating
epileptic seizures and knock-down of the Scn8a gene in the mouse brain reduces seizures. However, current
methods for knocking down Scn8a gene are based on antisense strategies, which are difficult to clinically implement
because they require repeated injections into the brain. Gene editing of the SCN8A gene has great promise to
address the above-mentioned concern and additionally can permit allele-specific inactivation of dominant pathogenic
allele in heterozygotes. Indeed, editing of a pathogenic Scn8a allele specifically has already been accomplished via
CRISPR, using AAV as a delivery vector and rescued heterozygous mice from epileptic seizures. However, AAV-
mediated gene editing in the brain is problematic because of prolonged expression of Cas9 as well as its
immunogenicity. There is consequently an urgent need to develop safe and efficient non-viral delivery vehicles that
can deliver CRISPR to the brain. Among non-viral delivery strategies, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have great potential
for delivering mRNA to the brain because of their well-characterized clinical track record and their versatility. However,
mRNA delivery to the brain with LNPs is currently inefficient because of limited diffusion in the brain and low levels of
endosomal disruption, and needs to be more efficient before it can generate significant therapeutics effects. To
address this critical need, we developed acid-degradable LNPs (termed ADP-LNPs), which are made with acid-
degradable polyethylene glycol (PEG) lipids and can transfect large volumes of brain tissue after an intracranial
injection, because they tolerate high levels of PEGylation without losing activity. Our preliminary results demonstrate
that ADP-LNPs deliver Cas9 mRNA to the brain with remarkable efficiency via an intracranial injection; ~5 times
higher gene editing efficiency than standard LNPs in the mouse brain. We have demonstrated that a single intracranial
injection of ADP-LNPs carrying Cas9 mRNA/Ai9 sgRNA could induce gene editing ~30% of the total cells in the
dentate gyrus (DG), a part of the hippocampus using Ai9 reporter mice. Additionally, we demonstrated that ADP-
LNPs carrying Cas9 mRNA/Scn8a sgRNA could reduce NaV1.6 expression levels by ~50% in 1/3 of the DG without
a sign of toxicity. These exciting results demonstrate that ADP-LNPs have great potential as precision-medicine
therapeutics for epilepsy. The central objectives of this proposal are (1) to develop new LNP variants based upon
ADP-LNPs with improved diffusion and efficiency, and (2) to develop a new therapeutic strategy for treating epileptic
seizures based upon local CRISPR/Cas9-mediated Scn8a gene editing in the mouse hippocampus using our newly
developed LNP-mRNA complexes. The central hypothesis is: intracerebral delivery of LNP-mRNA complexes that
carry Cas9 mRNA and sgRNA targeting the Scn8a gene can prevent/rescue mice from epileptic seizures.
Specific Aim 1. Increase the mouse brain gene editing efficiency of the ADP-LNPs
Specific Aim 2. Reduce seizures by knocking down Scn8a in a chemically-induced mouse seizure model
Specific Aim 3. Reduce seizures by knocking down the pathogenic Scn8a-N1768D allele in a mouse model of
pediatric seizures
The experiments in this proposal are significant because if successful, they will demonstrate that non-viral gene
editing of the Scn8a gene in the hippocampus can treat SCN8A-related epilepsies and will enable the development
of a new class of epilepsy therapeutics. These experiments are innovative given that they demonstrate that ADP-
LNPs provide two advantages over traditional LNPs: (1) enhanced diffusion in brain tissue and (2) enhanced
endosomal disruption, and have great potential for developing brain therapeutics that can deliver mRNA to large
volumes of brain tissue.
project_title: Gene editing therapeutics that prevent epileptic seizures
phr_text:
--------------------------------------------------------------Project Narrative-------------------------------------------------------------
The experiments in this proposal focus on developing lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mRNA complexes that can protect
mice from epileptic seizures via gene editing of a seizure causing gene. The LNP-mRNA complexes developed
in this proposal will edit large volumes of brain tissue non-virally and we propose to use them to treat mouse
models of seizure. If successful, the experiments in this proposal will develop a new strategy for treating seizures.
